slot.brief: Show a Fischer projection of a molecule with four different groups (figure) and ask for the R/S configuration at the stereocentre, with one distractor being a 180° rotation of the projection.

stem: What is the configuration at the stereocentre, and what configuration results from rotating the Fischer projection by $180^\circ$ in the plane? Use the figure.

verdicts.working: CIP priorities: OH (1) > NH₂ (2) > COOH (3) > CH₂OH (4). In the Fischer projection, group 4 is horizontal (toward the viewer); reversing the apparent sense gives R. A 180° in-plane rotation swaps both pairs and preserves configuration.

working:
CIP priorities: OH > NH2 > COOH > CH2OH; the carbon groups compare as [O,O,O] > [O,H,H].
Priority 1 is left, 2 is right, and 3 is bottom: $1\to2\to3$ is clockwise.
Priority 4 is on the vertical bond, so it points away: configuration is $(R)$.
A $180^\circ$ in-plane rotation preserves the configuration.

Independent check: CIP priorities: OH (1) > NH₂ (2) > COOH (3) > CH₂OH (4). In the Fischer projection, group 4 is horizontal (toward the viewer); reversing the apparent sense gives R. A 180° in-plane rotation swaps both pairs and preserves configuration.
solution:
CIP priority order is $$OH $>$ NH₂ $>$ COOH $>$ CH₂OH$$. With the lowest-priority group directed away, $1\to2\to3$ is clockwise, giving $(R)$.
A $180^\circ$ in-plane rotation of a Fischer projection preserves configuration; it remains $(R)$.
